headline: North America strength offsets a steep International slide
summary_short: Q4 net sales rose 6% year-over-year to $1.77 billion and topped full-year guidance, but net income fell 9% to $110 million as International segment Adjusted EBITDA plunged 81% on Middle East disruption and cost inflation.
summary_long: Full-year fiscal 2026 net sales rose 2% to $6.61 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.15 billion both topped guidance; Q4 net sales grew 6% on a sixth consecutive quarter of volume gains and an extra week, though price/mix and cost pressures cut margins. Net income fell to $110 million as North America segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 17% on volume and cost savings, while International Adjusted EBITDA fell 81% on EMEA competition, Middle East disruption and a $33 million potato write-off. Fiscal 2027 guidance: roughly flat-to-up-1% net sales, Adjusted EBITDA of $1.1-1.2 billion, Adjusted diluted EPS of $2.95-$3.25. Cash was $68 million; capex fell to $410 million.

drivers.explanation: Net sales grew on a sixth consecutive quarter of volume growth (+7%) and a 2% currency tailwind, plus an extra fiscal week, partly offset by a 3% price/mix decline from customer trade support and a mix shift toward faster-growing chain and private-label customers.

Gross profit rose in step with net sales (+5.6%) as gross margin held roughly flat at about 20.4% in both periods, per the reported cost-of-sales figures -- no separate gross-margin driver is disclosed.

Operating income fell as price/mix pressure and higher cost of sales and SG&A expenses outweighed volume gains; cost savings and operational improvements lowered manufacturing costs per pound but did not fully offset the decline.
Tracks the same cost and price pressures as operating income; the shard's EBIT figure is a Yahoo-derived measure that does not tie exactly to a single GAAP line item in the release.

Adds back the release's depreciation and amortization (about $106.0 million) to EBIT; declines for the same underlying reasons, since the company does not disclose a directly comparable unadjusted EBITDA line.

Net income fell as North America segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 17% on volume gains and cost savings, while International Adjusted EBITDA dropped 81% on EMEA competitive pressure, Middle East-linked disruption and a $33.1 million potato write-off.

Tracks the net-income decline; diluted weighted-average shares fell slightly to 138.0 million from 141.0 million year-over-year, a modest per-share tailwind that only partly cushioned the profit decline.
Tracks basic net income per share the same way; basic weighted-average shares fell to 137.7 million from 140.6 million year-over-year.

CEO Mike Smith cited 'Focus to Win' strategy progress and North America share gains, while noting Middle East conflict-related disruption and input cost inflation weighed on the International segment; the company also exceeded its $100 million fiscal-2026 cost-savings milestone.
